root_cause.text: The arm64 BPF JIT’s `check_imm()` macro in `arch/arm64/net/bpf_jit_comp.c` used `bits` instead of `bits - 1` when validating signed branch immediates, so it incorrectly accepted out-of-range displacements for `B`, `B.cond`, and `CBZ/CBNZ` encodings.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `((imm) >> (bits))` and `(~(imm) >> (bits))` to shift by `((bits) - 1)`, and the CVE text explains the old check admitted values in `[-2^N, 2^N)` for a signed N-bit field, letting `check_imm19()`/`check_imm26()` pass values that `aarch64_insn_encode_immediate()` then masked into the wrong branch target.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix immediate range validation in `check_imm()` to correctly detect values that exceed the signed bit-width limit.
intent_record.what: The `check_imm(bits, imm)` macro was changed so the range test shifts by `((bits) - 1)` instead of `bits` for both the positive and negative immediate-value checks.
intent_record.how: This makes the macro reject immediates that do not fit within the intended signed bit width, tightening the out-of-range detection by one bit compared to the previous logic.

grouping_result.intent: Fix immediate range validation in `check_imm()` to correctly detect values that exceed the signed bit-width limit.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes immediate range validation in `check_imm()`, which matches the root cause of using `bits` instead of `bits - 1` for signed branch immediates in the arm64 BPF JIT.

candidates.rationale: This positive-immediate check uses `bits` directly, which is off by one for signed branch immediates and can let out-of-range displacements pass validation.
This negative-immediate check also shifts by `bits` instead of `bits - 1`, so it fails to reject some signed branch offsets that exceed the legal encoding range.

vuln_statements.explanation: This part of `check_imm()` validates positive signed branch immediates using `bits` instead of `bits - 1`, which allows out-of-range displacements to be incorrectly accepted.
This part of `check_imm()` validates negative signed branch immediates using `bits` instead of `bits - 1`, so invalid branch offsets can pass range checking.
